strategic-advisory.name: Strategic Advisory
strategic-advisory.summary: Consulting-style advisory deck applying Minto's pyramid: title, situation/complication/question, the answer in one sentence, and three argued points with a process. Use when the audience expects a recommendation and the case for it, in that order.

beats.name: Title
beats.description: Open with a one-line summary statement that captures the recommendation, not the topic. The title slide is the headline of the entire engagement — make it specific enough that someone reading only this slide already understands the position.

beats.name: Situation, Complication, Question
beats.description: Frame the engagement on a single slide: the relevant status quo, what needs to change, and the question that needs to be resolved. This is the SCQ shorthand — context, tension, prompt. Don't yet answer.

beats.name: Answer
beats.description: Deliver the recommendation in a single sentence. No arguments yet, no caveats. The answer is the apex of the pyramid; the rest of the deck supports it.
beats.instructions: A solution in one sentence, no arguments yet

beats.name: Arguments
beats.description: Preview the three top-level arguments that defend the answer. One slide naming all three so the audience knows where the deck is going. Each argument should be a complete claim, not a topic.

beats.name: Argument 1
beats.description: Develop the first argument with supporting data, examples, and reasoning. Lead with the claim, then the evidence — Minto-style. The slide should stand alone if pulled out.

beats.name: Argument 2
beats.description: Develop the second argument the same way. Vary the type of evidence — quantitative, qualitative, comparative — so the audience hears the case from multiple angles.

beats.name: Argument 3
beats.description: Develop the third argument and walk through the supporting process or methodology. This is often where the 'how' lives — the implementation insight that makes the recommendation feel actionable.
beats.instructions: Third key point with a process

beats.name: Summary
beats.description: Recap the answer and arguments in a single slide and point to additional resources. Close with the explicit next step you want the audience to take.
beats.instructions: Recap the answer, provide additional resources

engineering-team.name: Engineering Team
engineering-team.summary: Practitioners building the system; they want depth, mechanism, and tradeoffs.
engineering-team.description: Engineers tune out generalities and tune in to specifics. Show benchmarks with conditions, architecture diagrams with constraints, and tradeoffs you actually considered. Internal jargon is fine — assume the room shares it. Leave room for questions; engineering audiences engage best when they can poke at the proposal.

investor.name: Investor
investor.summary: Angel investors, VCs, or institutional investors evaluating financial viability, market opportunity, and team.
investor.description: Angel, venture, and institutional investors judging financial viability, market opportunity, and the team. Lead with traction, size the market (TAM, SAM, SOM), make the moat and differentiation explicit, and show financial projections with their assumptions stated. Moderate chart density; 12-20 slides.

persuade.name: Persuade
persuade.summary: Change belief or win support for a specific argument, idea, or recommendation.
persuade.description: Use when the audience may be skeptical or undecided. Build a crisp thesis, support it with evidence, address objections, and end with a clear action.
persuade.outcome: The audience accepts the argument or supports the recommendation.

casual.name: Casual
casual.summary: Warm, plain-spoken voice for internal updates and customer storytelling.
casual.description: Friendly and direct. Use first- and second-person freely; favor short sentences and contractions. Numbers are still welcome — they just sit alongside human-scale framing rather than leading.
voiceCues: Favor short sentences and active voice.
Frame metrics with a human-scale anchor when possible.
samplePhrases: We shipped the new dashboard last week, and customers are already moving over.
Here's where we ended up on hiring this quarter.
It's been a busy month — here's the recap.

classic.name: Classic
classic.description: A timeless, clean, and versatile theme with balanced color contrasts and classic typography. Ideal for professional, readable presentations.

bold-red.name: Bold Red
bold-red.summary: Confident red and teal accents for urgent, high-salience stories.
bold-red.description: A bold red-led scheme with teal and navy support. Use it when the deck needs urgency, contrast, and clear emphasis.

cool-horizon.name: Cool Horizon
cool-horizon.summary: Cool blue-green palette tuned for professional business decks.
cool-horizon.description: A balanced cool-toned scheme with deep navy, business blues, and teal accents. It works well across strategy, finance, and technical narratives.

trebuchet-ms.name: Trebuchet MS
trebuchet-ms.description: Trebuchet MS is a sans serif OPF font scheme for Latin presentations, using Trebuchet MS for both headings and body text.

tenorite.name: Tenorite
tenorite.description: Tenorite is a sans serif OPF font scheme for Latin presentations, using Tenorite Display for headings with Tenorite for body text.

cover.name: Cover
cover.summary: The opening slide: title, subtitle and an optional picture.
cover.description: Open a presentation with its subject and a short introduction. Add a picture when it helps establish the context.

text.name: Text
text.summary: Prose. Several blocks sit side by side when short and stack when long.
text.description: Explain one idea in continuous prose. Use paragraphs or flowing blocks for detail that needs to be read in sequence.

chart.name: Chart
chart.summary: One to six charts, with an optional note.
chart.description: Give a chart enough space to show its evidence. Use the title to state the conclusion and labels to explain the measures.

table-beside.name: Table beside
table-beside.summary: A table with commentary beside it.
table-beside.description: Place a table beside its interpretation. Use the supporting text to explain the conclusion without repeating every cell.

timeline.name: Timeline
timeline.summary: Dated events or a roadmap along one axis, with optional notes.
timeline.description: Show events or milestones in chronological order. Label each item with a date or stage and a concise description.

list.name: List
list.summary: Bulleted or numbered points; one long list flows into columns.
list.description: Present several related points in a clear sequence. Use bullets for independent points or numbered items for an ordered list.
